{{Short description|American mathematician}}
{{for|the Hong Kong actor|Chapman To}}
'''Edward W Ng''' ({{zh|t=伍煒國}}; September 23, 1939 – December 14, 2018) was an American [[applied mathematician]] who had also held the positions of senior scientist, senior [[engineer]] and technical manager in the [[U.S. Space Program]]. He is noted for his broad variety of mathematical applications in [[space science]] and engineering. He has also contributed conscientiously in the spin-off of technology from the space program, with applications in such diverse subjects as [[Bose–Einstein distribution]] in [[mathematical physics]], [[symbolic and algebraic computation]], [[computational physics]] and [[biomedical research]].

Ng attended the [[Queen Elizabeth School, Hong Kong]] for secondary education, and the [[University of Minnesota]] for his [[bachelor's degree]]. He received his M.A. and [[doctorate|PhD]] degrees from [[Columbia University]]. He was employed at the [[Jet Propulsion Laboratory]] ([[JPL]]) of the [[California Institute of Technology]], a.k.a. [[Caltech]] under contract with the [[National Aeronautics and Space Administration]] ([[NASA]]). He retired in 2006.

Ng was elected a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (AAAS) and is cited in the [[American Men and Women of Science]].<ref>[http://www.gale-edit.com/amws/index.htm cf. Home page, AMWS] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081001220218/http://www.gale-edit.com/amws/index.htm |date=2008-10-01 }}, 25th ed. Vol.5, P.766 (2008)</ref> He was the editor of "Symbolic and Algebraic Computation" ({{isbn|3-540-09519-5}}),<ref>{{cite book | url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/3-540-09519-5 | doi=10.1007/3-540-09519-5 | title=Symbolic and Algebraic Computation | series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science | date=1979 | volume=72 | isbn=978-3-540-09519-4 }}</ref> in the [[Springer Science]] Lecture Notes Series. He was also a co-editor of the Proceedings of a [[NATO]] Advanced Study Institute in applied mathematics ({{isbn|978-90-277-1571-5}}).<ref>{{cite book | url=https://www.springer.com/computer/mathematics/book/978-90-277-1571-5 | title=Computational Aspects of Complex Analysis }}</ref>  He has published numerous technical papers of diverse mathematical applications in space sciences and engineering (selected list in external link below). His papers have appeared in [[Astrophysical Journal]], [[Mathematics of Computation]], [[Celestial Mechanics and Dynamical Astronomy]],<ref>[https://www.springer.com/astronomy/journal/10569 An International Journal in Space Dynamics]</ref> [[Journal of Computational Physics]], [[M.I.T.]] [[Journal of Mathematics and Physics]],<ref>renamed as [http://www.blackwellpublishing.com/journal.asp?ref=0022-2526  "Studies in Applied Mathematics"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080615205237/http://www.blackwellpublishing.com/journal.asp?ref=0022-2526 |date=2008-06-15 }}</ref> [[ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software]] and Proceedings of the [[American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics]].

==Notable quotes==
* "In science, one man's noise is another man's signal." cited in New York Times (1990).<ref name="nytimes">{{cite news|url=https://query.nytimes.com/gst/fullpage.html?res=9C0CE2DE1638F933A15750C0A966958260&sec=&spon=|title=Lost on Earth: Wealth of Data Found in Space - New York Times|accessdate=2014-05-27|newspaper=The New York Times|date=1990-03-20|last1=Blakeslee|first1=Sandra}}</ref> The context was in [[space science]] data and the reference was to the scientific-engineering concept of [[Signal-to-noise ratio]].
* ''Why Do We Explore Space?''<ref>[http://adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2006aiaa.conf.7313N doc entry at NASA Astrophysics Data System]</ref> an educational paper in '''Space 2006''',<ref>[http://arc.aiaa.org/doi/abs/10.2514/6.2006-7313] published by the [[American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics]]</ref>
* ''Nobel Connection to the Space Program'',<ref>[http://trs-new.jpl.nasa.gov/dspace/handle/2014/40971 NASA Document ID: 20080045909] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121124065513/http://trs-new.jpl.nasa.gov/dspace/handle/2014/40971 |date=2012-11-24 }}</ref> a paper in '''Space 2007''',<ref>[http://www.astrosociology.org/Library/PDF/Contributions/Space%202007%20Articles/The%20Nobel%20Connection%20to%20Space%20Program.pdf Space 2007] {{isbn|1-56347-888-9}}</ref> published by the [[American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics]].
* High-precision approximations of '''Bose–Einstein Functions'''<ref>''Mathematics of Computation'', Vol. 23, #107, [https://docs.google.com/fileview?id=0B_koTcZM3jtMNmM4M2M2ZTgtZDg4Zi00MTNiLTk0MTEtOWE2MzFhZjZhMGJh&hl=en view excerpts]</ref> in the ''[[Mathematics of Computation]]'' published by the [[American Mathematical Society]].
* Information Systems for '''Space Astrophysics'''* <ref>[https://ntrs.nasa.gov/search.jsp?R=19930017853&qs=N%3D0%26DocumentID%3D19930017853 Proceedings of Information Systems for Space Astrophysics]</ref>

==Awards==
Ng has received a number of NASA Awards (cf attached citations),<ref>[https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1ySDk5x25C59RNOEKHKIPJ3USAfI8MHGi2Srw8KavMnc/edit#slide=id.i0 (cf 6-page citations)]</ref> including the special NASA Certificate of Apollo-Columbia Commemoration of the Space Transportation System–65 Flight in 1994. He also was the recipient of the American Astronomical Society Team Appreciation Award on the [[Deep Space Network]].<ref>[https://drive.google.com/file/d/0B88DbO0F35P8blJRY1AyQUY0bEU/view?usp=sharing Ref: mathematics for Deep Space Network]</ref>
